label: Darwall proposes that moral obligation involves answerability to legitimate demanders
paraphrase: On Darwall's account, if an all-things-considered moral obligation binds an agent, its violation without adequate excuse makes that agent morally answerable to an authorized claimant or moral community. The authority may belong to a moral community or, on some theistic readings, God: the claim does not by itself give the particular victim exclusive authority or assert that moral obligations exist.
